item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-b89e895b33cb81f8","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 30 January 2023, Mexico's National Electoral Institute (INE) reported that its Executive Secretariat had presented an assessment of how the decrees comprising the Plan B electoral reform affected electoral functions.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.4","4B.10","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns a 2023 electoral reform initiative; the supplied unit does not state the reform's ultimate legal or operational outcome.","ruler_attribution":"The document describes an executive-supported legislative/decree package but does not expressly attribute the decrees to López Obrador personally.","limitations":["The supplied extraction does not include the substantive findings of the INE report, only its presentation and purpose."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3bfedc0df1f21dc6","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"A 2023 University of Guanajuato article reviewed scholarship on political clientelism in Mexico from 2007 to 2022 and stated that economic deprivation enables political leaders and parties to establish clientelist relationships, which affect local democracy.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.5","4B.7","5B.1","5B.5","5B.8","6B.3","6B.7","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Published in 2023 but reviews literature covering 2007–2022; it provides general national context rather than a specific 2023 finding about López Obrador.","ruler_attribution":"No direct attribution to López Obrador or his administration in the supplied units.","limitations":["The extraction gives only the article metadata and abstract, not its detailed findings or evidence about particular programs, parties, or regions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1e77a4d318aa7b0e","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL's 2023 results report stated that the average fulfillment of targets across its indicators was 106%; 96% advanced as programmed and 4% exceeded the programmed target. It also reported that 95% of improvement actions for federal social-development programs were completed, 95% of coordinated federal-program evaluations were disseminated, 99% of surveyed decision-makers were satisfied with CONEVAL analyses and recommendations, use of CONEVAL information increased 34% relative to the 2012–2022 average, and 173 mandated evaluations were coordinated.","question_ids":["5B.7","6B.5","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Reports CONEVAL institutional performance and evaluation activity during 2023; it does not by itself establish outcomes of all government social programs.","ruler_attribution":"These are results of CONEVAL, a federal evaluation institution, during López Obrador's administration; the supplied unit does not establish which outcomes were personally directed by him.","limitations":["The report concerns monitoring and evaluation outputs rather than direct welfare outcomes, distributional incidence, or independent assessment of policy quality."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1acd6378bf8d0e18","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"A 2023 economics paper described energy security as involving trade-offs between affordability and reliability, and stated that the transition to carbon-free energy creates new security challenges, including dependence on different resources, redundant capital stock, undercapitalized energy companies, and regulatory uncertainty that deters investment.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.4","5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Published 18 January 2023 and addresses general energy-policy conditions during geopolitical and environmental crises; it does not present Mexico-specific evidence or evaluate López Obrador's actions.","ruler_attribution":"No attribution to López Obrador or Mexico in the supplied units.","limitations":["The supplied extraction contains only the abstract and bibliographic material, not country-specific findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-34e64a180252982a","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"México Evalúa's Hallazgos 2023 stated that Mexico's approved judicial reform did not center access to justice or protection of rights, and that available evidence suggested it would not improve the right to justice; the organization characterized it as politically driven and said Mexico's criminal-justice system continued to have significant deficiencies with serious consequences for rights.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.10","4B.2","4B.4","4B.10","7B.6","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The page is dated 31 October 2024 but presents Hallazgos 2023 and evaluates a reform associated with the period; the supplied text does not specify enactment dates or López Obrador's personal role.","ruler_attribution":"The document discusses an approved judicial reform during the relevant political period but does not expressly identify López Obrador as its author or decision-maker.","limitations":["The supplied extraction summarizes México Evalúa's assessment without the underlying indicators, methodology tables, or detailed attribution of responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-81f666c82d1b26fa","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"A study of Mexico reported that femicide laws did not reduce femicides, homicides, disappearances, or suicides of women, and that results remained robust across alternative legal reforms; it concluded that laws were insufficient against gender-based violence in contexts of impunity.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.7","3B.10","6B.8","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The study was submitted in 2024 and evaluates legal variation across Mexico; it is relevant as later evidence about the effectiveness of legal protections but is not a contemporaneous 2023 report.","ruler_attribution":"No direct attribution to López Obrador; the study evaluates laws and state-level variation rather than presidential direction.","limitations":["The supplied abstract does not identify which laws were enacted or implemented during López Obrador's 2023 administration, nor does it establish personal responsibility for the observed outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cb795e81bad8fa61","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"Mexicanos Contra la Corrupción y la Impunidad and Nexos reported that López Obrador described the diversion of more than 15 billion pesos from Segalmex as the only corruption case in his administration and acknowledged it in December 2023. The report stated that procurement irregularities had been flagged as early as April 2019, that diversions were documented by 2020 and subsequently accumulated, and that the authors identified 32 corruption cases in 2023, most involving the federal government or governing coalition.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.1","7B.2","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers corruption reporting and presidential statements through 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The document directly attributes the quoted characterization and December 2023 acknowledgment to López Obrador; allegations about broader cases and selective justice are the authors' assessment.","limitations":["This is an advocacy and investigative accountability publication; the supplied extraction does not provide final judicial findings for all 32 cases or independently adjudicate each allegation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0b2b61187b86f768","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"UNICEF identified its 15 November 2023 Mexico Humanitarian Situation Report on Hurricane Otis as a situation report monitoring the humanitarian response, children's needs, and funding requirements.","question_ids":["3B.9","3B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly concerns the November 2023 Hurricane Otis emergency, but the supplied extraction contains only the report description and no substantive findings.","ruler_attribution":"The report concerns Mexico's humanitarian situation and response but does not attribute specific decisions to López Obrador in the supplied unit.","limitations":["The linked PDF's substantive contents were not supplied, so no concrete claims about government preparedness, resource allocation, or outcomes can be made."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6a09387bfe7713d5","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"A study using Mexican homicide, missing-person, arrest, and cartel-interaction data estimated that cartels had 160,000–185,000 members by 2022 and recruited at least 350 people per week. It reported that increasing current levels of state incapacitation would increase homicides and cartel membership, while reducing recruitment through proactive investment targeting at-risk individuals would substantially reduce violence and cartel population.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","6B.3","6B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Submitted 2 February 2023 and uses data through 2022; it offers policy-relevant baseline and causal-model evidence rather than a direct evaluation of 2023 implementation.","ruler_attribution":"No direct attribution to López Obrador or his administration; the paper evaluates alternative national violence-reduction strategies.","limitations":["The supplied abstract does not report whether Mexico adopted the proposed recruitment-reduction strategy in 2023 or its subsequent effects."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-53e288fa08d8e80e","SRC-c675c9b8f73634ff","SRC-8946a434ef8ab22a"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied documents contain only webpage shells, access errors, bibliographic metadata, or abstracts; facts are limited to the extracted units.","The supplied material does not support a comprehensive assessment of all 1B–8B questions and should not be used to infer scores.","Some sources concern general Mexico context or later evaluations rather than López Obrador's directly attributable 2023 decisions."]}
